class.name: Box3DFilterJoint
class.brief_description: Stops two specific bodies colliding with each other, and nothing else.
class.description: The cheapest joint in Box3D: it applies no constraint at all. Its only effect is that [member body_a] and [member body_b] stop colliding with each other while staying in the same simulation island. This is the case collision layers and masks cannot express: two bodies that share a layer, must keep colliding with everything else on it, and must ignore only each other -- a character and the crate it is carrying, two links of a chain that overlap by design, a turret and the hull it sits on. Both bodies are required. Unlike the other joint types, leaving [member body_b] empty does not anchor anything to the world, it just leaves the joint with nothing to filter. Inherited settings that describe a constraint ([member Box3DJoint.constraint_hertz], the spring and threshold properties) have no effect here, because there is no constraint to tune.
